data.name: Pralay
data.gender_notes: Pralay is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Pralay refers to the deluge or cataclysm that marks the end of a cycle of creation and the beginning of a new one. The name Pralay carries the meaning “The Deluge or Cataclysm” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Pralay usually hope their child will grow to embody the deluge or cataclysm and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Pralay belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “The Deluge or Cataclysm.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Pralay total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Pralay" holds significance as it reflects the cycle of destruction and rebirth ingrained in Hindu beliefs. It represents the end of an era and the birth of a new one.
data.spiritual_significance: The word "Pralay" holds immense spiritual significance in Hinduism. According to Hindu scriptures, Pralay is the cosmic flood or deluge, a divine intervention that signals the end of an age and the beginning of a new one. This symbolizes the continuous cycle of death and rebirth, which is a fundamental aspect of Hinduism.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Pralay signifies the cycle of destruction and creation in the universe, representing the end of one cosmic era and the beginning of another. It is a reminder of the transient nature of life and the inevitability of change.

vedic_reference.root_origin: Sanskrit root लय (laya) - dissolution, merging, destruction
vedic_reference.note: Not directly from Vedas or Upanishads but originates from a Sanskrit root.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu epic Mahabharata describes a great cosmic battle called the Mahabharata War, which ultimately leads to the destruction of the world as described in the text of the Mahabharata. This event is referred to as Pralay in Hindu mythology.
historical_references.context: An ancient Indian text recounting the epic struggle between good and evil, featuring many gods and heroes.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu scripture Bhagavata Purana describes the repeated cycle of creation and destruction of the universe. Each cycle is called a Pralaya, and is brought about by the god Vishnu in his avatar as Mahavishnu.
historical_references.context: A foundational Hindu text detailing the cosmic cycles of creation and destruction

modern_usage.modern_context: In Hindu mythology, Pralay refers to the cataclysmic event of a cosmic deluge that destroys the world and then paves the way for its creation anew. This concept has found its way into various modern contexts, including the scientific discourse on climate change and natural disasters, science fiction, and pop culture. In the context of climate change, the term 'Pralay' is often used metaphorically to describe the potential end of the world due to rising temperatures, melting ice caps, and extreme weather events. In science fiction, Pralay is a popular trope where an alien invasion, supervolcanic eruption, or other catastrophic events bring about the end of the world, only to be followed by a new beginning. Lastly, in pop culture, references to Pralay can be found in various movies, TV shows, and video games, such as 'Waterworld,' 'The Day After Tomorrow,' and 'Fallout.'
